extracted.intended_audience: scholars, students, and practitioners in media studies, journalism, and communication; media managers interested in news production and online newswork
extracted.subtask_description: Publisher book page describing a scholarly study (News at Work) of imitation and homogenization in contemporary news production and consumption, based on comparative empirical research in Buenos Aires and the U.S.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rigorous scholarship
rubrics_metrics.description: The work exhibits rigorous scholarship and methodological care.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviews emphasize Boczkowski's 'reputation for rigorous scholarship' and note the use of both qualitative and quantitative analysis; Appendix A: Research Design and Appendix B: Supplementary Studies indicate transparency about methods and empirical grounding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Empirical access and comparative case study
rubrics_metrics.description: Close, inside access to news organizations and comparative analysis across contexts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The book compares and contrasts two newspapers in Buenos Aires with similar developments in the United States and is praised for 'close access to the leading news organizations in Buenos Aires,' which supports claims about newsroom practices and imitation dynamics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explanation of imitation/homogenization
rubrics_metrics.description: Provides a novel, parsimonious explanation for why news stories look similar across outlets and how imitation operates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Characterized in reviews as offering 'a novel, parsimonious explanation' and explicating 'the imitative life cycle' through accounts of production, technology use, and consumption; a criterion for strength is explanatory clarity about mechanisms of imitation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Linking production, distribution, and consumption
rubrics_metrics.description: Analyzes the connections among news production processes, distribution systems, and audience consumption practices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Described as giving 'a panoramic view of the links between the production, distribution, and consumption of digital media' — strong work should integrate these dimensions rather than treating them separately (chapters cover production, product homogenization, and consumption at work).

rubrics_metrics.name: Attention to newsroom labor and practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Detailed examination of editorial labor, monitoring, and imitation within newsrooms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The book documents how rival news organizations 'keep tabs on the competition and imitate them,' explores 'monitoring and imitation in news production,' and explains why journalists contribute to growing similarity even if they dislike it; criteria include descriptive depth about routines, technologies, and decision-making.

rubrics_metrics.name: Empirical demonstration of homogenization and decreased diversity
rubrics_metrics.description: Evidence that online news availability and newsroom imitation lead to decreased diversity of news content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The central claim is that increased information abundance coincides with a 'decrease in the diversity of the news' and 'the homogenization of news products'; evaluative strength depends on empirical measures and documented examples of content similarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relevance and timeliness to digital media era
rubrics_metrics.description: Addresses contemporary changes in how news is produced and consumed in an age of constant online updates and workplace reading.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes that most people now follow headlines at work and that the Internet transforms breaking news into a homogenized commodity; valuable work demonstrates relevance to current digital practices and their consequences for journalism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bread and ambition of scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Ambitious, multi-dimensional inquiry covering production, content, and consumption.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviews call it an 'exceptionally ambitious study' analyzing 'different dimensions of news' — criteria include the book's ability to cover multiple levels (organizational, textual, audience) coherently and to provoke scholarly debate.
